segments.en:
Part 4 (§§ 37–50 / Oaseyos לז–נ)

COMPLETE · Based on LM I:24 (Amtza'isa D'Alma)

§ 37 — Notzair [Guards] = Ratzon [Will]: The Inflaming of Truth Through Desire

Notzair [guards/preserves] is the letters of ratzon [will] — for the essential thing is the will, as explained in our writings extensively. This is the essential illumination of the inflaming of truth in the heart: the truth should illuminate and inflame in his heart always, in gradation and measure, until his will is strong always for Hashem, His Torah, and His true tzadikim — this is the essential thing, as above. Therefore, when one reaches the aspect of Notzair Chesed [the eighth of the thirteen midos of mercy], no further open kindling is needed, as above — one cannot illuminate further in the open. The essential tikun is through the strong will, which shines even more through the inflaming of truth — the aspect of Yosef, as above.

§ 38 — Yosef's True Dreams and Interpreting Others' Dreams: Sleep, Sadness, and Exile

Therefore Yosef the tzadik merited true and accurate dreams, and also knew how to interpret the dreams of others during their sleep. Sleep is one-sixtieth of death, and sadness is the side of death. The essential sleep comes from the wearying of the mind. The root of holy sleep (= the sleep of the tzadikim) derives from the pursuit and obstructer: the mind pursues to perceive, the obstructer obstructs until it settles, etc. — through which the nine chambers are fashioned, and one perceives the Ain Sof light. Even though these nine chambers do not cling and are not known — from there all the holy mental faculties of the true tzadikim derive, for they are the lights of the tzachtzachos [brilliant splendors] — the root of all the midos, from which all mental faculties descend through the tzimtzumim and vessels the tzadikim fashion through their good deeds.

However, due to the wearying of the mind through the pursuit and obstructer, one must sleep to give the mind rest. Then specifically, during sleep, the tzadik sorts even more from the Chambers of Exchange, his soul ascends — the mind rising to where it rises, perceiving then what it perceives. This is the aspect of what is explained above (ois kaf-daled) in Parshas Vayaitzai: "he encountered the place... he lodged there... he dreamt" etc.; see there. Therefore one must take care to fall asleep amidst words of Torah, in order to sleep amidst joy — so that one does not taste the taste of death. This is David's plea: "illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death." And it was established for every person to say before sleep in Birchas HaMapil: "illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death" — as above.

This is connected to: "how long shall I set counsel in my soul, sorrow in my heart by day? How long shall my enemy be exalted over me?" — followed by "look... illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death." He cried: since exile overpowers so greatly — its essence being sorrow and sadness ("sorrow in my heart by day") — I plead: "illuminate my eyes, lest I sleep the death" — that Hashem illuminate his eyes so he can gladden his soul, so his sleep will not be in the aspect of the side of death (= sorrow and sadness). The four times "how long" David cried in this mizmor correspond to the four exiles, as Rashi explains. The essence of all exiles is sadness. David cried and prayed that Israel be saved from sorrow and sadness — that their enemies not be exalted over them through this, chas v'shalom, that they not sleep the death.

Therefore immediately follows: "but I trusted in Your kindness; my heart shall exult in Your salvation; I shall sing to Hashem" etc. He strengthened himself and all the souls of Israel encompassed in him: he trusts in His kindness, and through this gladdens himself — "my heart shall exult in Your salvation." This is the essential tikun for every person: to strengthen his heart in great trust in Hashem's kindnesses — certainly He will not abandon him — until he rejoices and exults: "my heart shall exult in Your salvation."

But those who do not merit this — their sleep is seized by the side of death according to their flaw in the mind, and their dreams are confused, etc. (holy Zohar). Every flaw of the mind and da'as is due to the flaw of the Arranger and Settler — one does not merit the power of the Arranger and Settler of the mind as needed. If one had proper yishuv hada'as [settled mind], certainly he would not pursue follies and unbecoming actions. As explained elsewhere (LM I:10): the essential distancing from Hashem is due to lacking yishuv hada'as. And: the essential yishuv hada'as is through joy, etc.; see there.

One depends on the other: because one does not overpower with joy — at least being grateful for being saved, for not being made a gentile, for being separated from those who err in many aspects, etc. — through this the mind is in exile. The more the exile of the mind overpowers, the more sadness overpowers; and so on. From this comes all distancing from Hashem. The tikun is the true tzadik (= Yosef), who knows in the depth of his wisdom how to gladden Jewish souls wherever they are, as above. Therefore he could interpret dreams — he could sort the good from the bad in the Chambers of Exchange, knowing the dream's interpretation even for common people, whose confusion derives from the Chambers of Exchange. He knew how to sort all this, as above.

segments.he: תפלת ערבית רשות והאדנא קבעוה עלייהו חובה על פי מה שכתב רבנו במאמר פתח רבי שמעון בסימן ס שעל ידי יראה זוכין לעשירות גדול, שעל ידי העשירות הזאת באין להתבוננות התורה. כי על ידי יראה מכניעין בחינת שקר החן והבל היפי עין שם היטב:
segments.en:
§ 39 — Yosef Interprets Pharaoh's Dream: The Seven Fat and Lean Years

Therefore Yosef knew how to interpret Pharaoh's dream, and through this emerged from exile and slavery. Pharaoh — king of Egypt, the first exile — derives from the sin of Adam HaRishon, when sadness was drawn (the side of death): "in sadness you shall eat it... until you return to the ground." Pharaoh saw the seven lean cows swallowing the seven fat cows (and the ears of grain, etc.): "they came into their insides and it was not known they had come" — sadness and sorrow overpowering the good, which is the aspect of satiation, blessing, and joy (as Rashi explains on "the meadows are clothed with flocks... they shout for joy, they also sing" — a shout of joy). But the seven years of famine (= the opposite: wailing and sadness, as in Yoel's decree of famine — "weep and wail... wail over the wheat and barley") overpower so greatly that they want to swallow and conceal Israel's joy entirely: "it was not known they had come" — the essential prolonging of exile, as above.

The essential sadness is in the matter of money, livelihood, and wealth — where the core sadness resides: "in sadness you shall eat it." Even one who has wealth constantly lacks more and worries more than the poor: "the more possessions, the more worry" — "it was not known they had come." Egypt is the aspect of the craving for money, as explained elsewhere. The tikun is Yosef the tzadik, who knows how to draw joy even in the depth of exile, interpreting the dream so we have sustenance: "G-d sent me before you for sustenance, to preserve for you a remnant on earth." All the events between Yosef and Pharaoh, between Yosef and his brothers, etc. — all allude to the length of this exile until the wondrous end, as is known.

Therefore it says of Yosef: "can there be found such a man, in whom the spirit of G-d resides?" — who knows how to blow and fan the dust from the Jewish heart, as above. "After G-d has made all this known to you, there is none as understanding and wise as you" — since you can interpret such a dream and rectify it (because you can sort the Chambers of Exchange through overpowering with joy through your deep counsel). As stated in the Midrash (Parshah 86) on "he was a successful man": the word implies leaping and dancing — even in his slavery in the prison he leaped and succeeded in gladdening his soul. The essential counsel: to gladden oneself with foolish things, as explained in our writings extensively. Therefore Pharaoh said: "after G-d has made all this known to you" — certainly "there is none as understanding and wise as you" — for you certainly merit the blessing of intellect attained through sorting the Chambers of Exchange through overpowering with joy, as above.

§ 40 — "Only the Throne Shall I Make Greater": The Obstructer Above Even the Tzadik

"You shall be over my house, and by your word all my people shall be sustained; only the throne shall I make greater than you." The tzadik (= Yosef), who merits ascending from the Chambers of Exchange through all the above ascents, merits all the above blessings and draws all bounty — physical and spiritual — to all the world: "you shall be over my house; by your word all my people shall be sustained" — all bounty drawn through you. "Only the throne shall I make greater than you" — the aspect of kisa d'miskasia [the concealed throne], Keser, the obstructer: "I shall be greater" — that your thought not pursue excessively; may you merit the Settler and Arranger, who obstructs the mind — Keser, the concealed throne, as explained (LM I:6).

This is also: "I am Pharaoh; without you no man shall raise his hand or foot" — raising hands and feet, the totality of all the above tikunim: raising the feet to walk and arouse all worlds to Hashem, drawing blessing (= the hands). But nonetheless — "I am Pharaoh." This parallels "only the throne shall I make greater," as Rashi explains there.

All this alludes to what the Torah above explains: one who merits sorting the Chambers of Exchange, ascending, etc. — attaining the blessing of intellect, the mind pursuing to perceive — his essential tikun is through the obstructer (= Keser, "only the throne"). This itself is "I am Pharaoh," as above. The Midrash (Parshah 90) states: "Raish Lakish said: two passages Moshe wrote us in the Torah, and we learn them from wicked Pharaoh. One verse says: 'you shall be only above' — could it mean like Me? The verse teaches: 'only' — My greatness is above yours. And we learn this from Pharaoh: 'you shall be...' — could it mean like me? 'Only' — my greatness is above yours. Likewise: 'you shall be holy' — like Me? 'For I am holy, Hashem your G-d' — My holiness is above your holiness. We learn this from Pharaoh: 'I am Pharaoh' — my greatness is above yours."

This is clear to one who understands and examines the above Torah: even though the tzadik (= Yosef) merited sorting as he merited until attaining the blessing of the mind (the mind pursuing, etc.) — nevertheless, he must not break through to Hashem. His entire tikun is through the obstructer (= Keser, "only the throne") — "I am Hashem; My holiness is above..."; he must not break through. Earthly kingship mirrors heavenly kingship — as the Midrash states: we learn from Pharaoh regarding the awesome holiness of Hashem, as above.

§ 41 — Avraich: The Tikunim Alluded to in Yosef's Title

"They called before him: Avraich." Avraich alludes to the above tikunim. Avraich = "a father to the king" — the tikun of Malchus, as above. Avraich = knees [birkayim] (as Rashi explains) — the tikun of the feet. Avraich = blessing [berachah] — the blessing of the hands. Avraich = av in wisdom, etc. — the blessing of intellect and wisdom. This is the aspect of Tzafnas Pa'anayach — "revealer of hidden things." He merits the above nine chambers that do not cling and are not known — from which all awesome, concealed secrets and mysteries are perceived.

segments.he: והנה יעקב שהוא בחינת יראה, כמו שאיתא בזהר 'ביראתך' בזכות יעקב שאמר מה נורא. ועל כן לא היה מתירא כלל מבחינת הבל היפי. ועל כן לא מצינו ביעקב שיאסר עליו זווגו אפלו בשעה שירד למצרים, כי אם אדרבא ה' יתברך הבטיחו אנכי ארד עמך מצרימה ואנכי אעלך וכו'. כי יעקב מטתו שלמה והיה שומר הברית ביותר ולא היה לו שום אחיזה ופחד מבחינת הבל היפי. וכל זה היה מחמת שזכה לבחינת יראה שהיא מכנעת בחינת הבל היפי כנזכר לעיל. ומחמת זה זכה יעקב לעשירות מפלג מאד כמו שכתוב ופרצת ימה וקדמה וכו' הינו נחלה בלי מצרים הינו בחינת כל הון דעלמא, כי כל האבות זכו לעשירות גדול לפי בחינת יראתם לפי בחינת הכנעתם את הבל היפי. אבל יעקב שהיה שלמות היראה וזכה להכניע לגמרי בחינת הבל היפי כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן זכה לתכלית העשירות, הינו כל הון דעלמא, נחלה בלי מצרים כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן תפלת ערבית רשות. כי תפלת ערבית היא בחינת יעקב, כי הוא תקנה, והוא בחינת יראה כנזכר לעיל שעל ידה זוכין לעשירות גדול, שעל ידה זוכין להתבוננות גדול הנזכרת לעיל. ועל כן היא רשות, כי כשזוכין להתבוננות הזאת אזי אין חובה להתפלל. כי זה ההתבוננות היא בחינת השגת רבי שמעון בן יוחאי שזכה לזה. ועל כן היה פטור מתפלה כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה . כי התבוננות הזאת היא בחינת 'תורתו אמנותו'. הינו שכל אמנות והעשירות שלו הוא רק מהתורה, בחינת פסלת של לוחות שמשם נתעשר משה, כמו שכתב אדוננו מורנו ורבנו שם עין שם. וזה שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה לא שנו אלא כגון רבי שמעון בן יוחאי וחבריו שתורתן אמנותן וכו'. ולפי פשוטו תמוה, כי הלא גם עתה נמצאים בני אדם שאין להם שום אמנות רק עוסקים בתורה, מכל שכן וכל שכן בימי הש"ס. אך העקר תלוי בהתבוננות הנזכרת לעיל שתלוי בעשירות. ועל כן נקרא תורתן אמנותן כנזכר לעיל:
segments.en:
§ 42 — "Do Not Be Saddened": Gathering to the Tzadik = Joy

"Now, do not be saddened." Since they merited gathering together to the true tzadik (= Yosef), certainly there is no more cause for sadness — only great joy: "when the righteous multiply, the people rejoice." Whoever comes to the tzadik within the gathering is in the category of a tzadik: "your people are all righteous" — with them is the source of joy: "rejoice, tzadikim, in Hashem"; "sing joyfully, tzadikim, in Hashem." But due to the bitterness of exile (general and personal), the aspect of tzadik within each person is concealed. However, as soon as they gather to the tzadik — "a man in whom there is spirit" — the point of tzadik in each one is illuminated. Through this, joy increases: "the light of the righteous makes glad" (as explained in the Torah "Chadi Rabbi Shimon," LM I:61, on this verse).

Therefore then: "the spirit of Yaakov their father was revived" — vitality and joy. As it says: "my son Yosef is yet alive — great!" Rashi explains: "great is my joy and gladness" etc. The essential joy — truth and holy emunah — all vitality and joy — comes essentially through the children one begets: through this Israel multiplies, the aspect of "a wise son gladdens a father"; "may the father rejoice in his offspring." Holy emunah must be revealed from generation to generation — this is the essential joy. "Serve Hashem with joy... know that Hashem is G-d" — the essential joy — concluding: "from generation to generation is His faithfulness." "I shall sing of Hashem's kindnesses forever; from generation to generation I shall make known Your faithfulness."

The essential joy in Him — begun by Avraham who first revealed emunah in the world — was primarily revealed through Yaakov, whose bed was complete (twelve tribes, all tzadikim). With each tribe born, joy increased. But the essential inflaming of joy's light was through Yosef's birth, as above. Yet the ba'al davar provoked greatly — creating dispute among them, a great flaw in joy. The essential joy is through love and peace: "for with joy you shall go out and in peace be led." The essential thing: Israel gathering together to the tzadik (= Yosef) — through which comes the essential joy, as above.

§ 43 — Binyamin's Portion: The Bais HaMikdash as the Place of Joy

Therefore the climax came through Binyamin — the Bais HaMikdash was in his portion, the holy, awesome Place where one can receive this holy light of joy. In truth, the essential completeness of joy is through all the above tikunim — drawn through the true tzadik who gladdens Jewish souls, who sort from the Chambers of Exchange and ascend, etc. — the mind pursuing, the Arranger obstructing, etc. — the nine chambers fashioned through the pursuit and obstructer (= Keser), where the source of joy resides: "eternal joy upon their heads."

But this joy is extremely difficult to bear in this world — it is above nefesh, ruach, neshamah, etc. One needs the awesome Place — the Bais HaMikdash — deriving at its root from "that Place" (= Keser, called Place): "blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place"; "he encountered the place" (Yaakov — ois kaf-daled above). This Place was Binyamin the tzadik's portion. Though Yosef was born and could gladden Israel, the holy bed was not complete until Binyamin was born in Eretz Yisrael. No place in the world can bear this light of joy — rejoicing in Him, which is beyond expression: each person according to what he can measure in his heart. Only the place of the Bais HaMikdash, where the source of joy is: "the King has brought me into His chambers — we shall exult and rejoice in You." From there joy flows to all Israel, each according to his good deeds — and essentially according to his closeness to the true tzadikim, who can gladden even the very worst, transforming sorrow and sighing to joy.

§ 44 — In Exile: The Tzadik's Da'as Replaces the Bais HaMikdash; Ben Oni / Binyamin

Now, in exile with the Bais HaMikdash destroyed, joy is extremely difficult — except through the power of tzadikim with great, wondrous da'as, considered equivalent to the building of the Bais HaMikdash: "whoever has da'as..." etc. They draw upon us joy in Him so we can survive this bitter exile.

Therefore his mother named him Ben Oni [son of my mourning] — Rachel died then and was buried at the crossroads, so Israel could weep at her grave during the destruction, as our Sages say. Rachel, seeing the great destruction that would come before the final end, named him Ben Oni — for the great mourning and weeping needed every midnight over the destruction of the Bais HaMikdash. Every person must cry out and weep each day over his flaws that delay the Bais HaMikdash's rebuilding: "a voice is heard on high, lamentation, bitter weeping — Rachel weeps for her children."

But his father called him Binyamin — for Eretz Yisrael: Yaakov called him "son of the right" for the ultimate end, when we return to Eretz Yisrael and the Bais HaMikdash is built in Binyamin's portion — where the source of joy resides. Yaakov said: even now he should be called Binyamin (= Eretz Yisrael = joy). Even now in exile, it is forbidden to be in sadness — one must cry out and pour out his heart for some time each day, but the rest of the day be in joy, gladdening his soul through all the counsel. Through joy comes the essential sorting from the Chambers of Exchange — through which one specifically leaves the exile, each according to his level: "for with joy you shall go out," as above.
segments.he_nikud: וְהִנֵּה יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יִרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר 'בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ' בִּזְכוּת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁאָמַר מַה נּוֹרָא. וְעַל-כֵּן לֹא הָיָה מִתְיָרֵא כְּלָל מִבְּחִינַת הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי. וְעַל-כֵּן לֹא מָצִינוּ בְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁיֵּאָסֵר עָלָיו זִוּוּגוֹ אֲפִלּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁיָּרַד לְמִצְרַיִם, כִּי אִם אַדְּרַבָּא ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחוֹ אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרָיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ וְכוּ'. כִּי יַעֲקֹב מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה וְהָיָה שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית בְּיוֹתֵר וְלֹא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם אֲחִיזָה וּפַחַד מִבְּחִינַת הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי. וְכָל זֶה הָיָה מֵחֲמַת שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְחִינַת יִרְאָה שֶׁהִיא מַכְנַעַת בְּחִינַת הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וּמֵחֲמַת זֶה זָכָה יַעֲקֹב לַעֲשִׁירוּת מֻפְלָג מְאֹד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְכוּ' הַיְנוּ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת כָּל הוֹן דְּעָלְמָא, כִּי כָּל הָאָבוֹת זָכוּ לַעֲשִׁירוּת גָּדוֹל לְפִי בְּחִינַת יִרְאָתָם לְפִי בְּחִינַת הַכְנָעָתָם אֶת הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי. אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהָיָה שְׁלֵמוּת הַיִּרְאָה וְזָכָה לְהַכְנִיעַ לְגַמְרֵי בְּחִינַת הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן זָכָה לְתַכְלִית הָעֲשִׁירוּת, הַיְנוּ כָּל הוֹן דְּעָלְמָא, נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת. כִּי תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית הִיא בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב, כִּי הוּא תִּקְּנָהּ, וְהוּא בְּחִינַת יִרְאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל שֶׁעַל יָדָהּ זוֹכִין לַעֲשִׁירוּת גָּדוֹל, שֶׁעַל-יָדָהּ זוֹכִין לְהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת גָּדוֹל הַנִּזְכֶּרֶת לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן הִיא רְשׁוּת, כִּי כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לַהִתְָבּוֹנְנוּת הַזֹּאת אֲזַי אֵין חוֹבָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל. כִּי זֶה הַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הִיא בְּחִינַת הַשָּגַת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי שֶׁזָּכָה לָזֶה. וְעַל-כֵּן הָיָה פָּטוּר מִתְּפִלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. כִּי הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הַזֹּאת הִיא בְּחִינַת 'תּוֹרָתוֹ אֻמָּנוּתוֹ'. הַיְנוּ שֶׁכָּל אֻמָּנוּת וְהָעֲשִׁירוּת שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא רַק מֵהַתּוֹרָה, בְּחִינַת פְּסֹלֶת שֶׁל לוּחוֹת שֶׁמִּשָּׁם נִתְעַשֵּׁר מֹשֶׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב אֲדוֹנֵנוּ מוֹרֵנוּ וְרַבֵּנוּ שָׁם עַיֵּן שָׁם. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי וַחֲבֵרָיו שֶׁתּוֹרָתָן אֻמָּנוּתָן וְכוּ'. וּלְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ תָּמוּהַּ, כִּי הֲלֹא גַּם עַתָּה נִמְצָאִים בְּנֵי-אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם אֻמָּנוּת רַק עוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה, מִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בִּימֵי הַשַּׁ"ס. אַךְ הָעִקָּר תָּלוּי בַּהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הַנִּזְכֶּרֶת לְעֵיל שֶׁתָּלוּי בַּעֲשִׁירוּת. וְעַל-כֵּן נִקְרָא תּוֹרָתָן אֻמָּנוּתָן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:

segments.he: ועל-כן יעקב תקן תפלת ערבית דיקא. כי אז בלילה הזמן מסגל יותר להשגות והתבוננות כמו שכתוב בש"ט שרב חדושי תורה זוכין בלילה. וכמו שכתב רבנו (בסימן נב) שבלילה מסגל יותר לבטול עין שם. גם הלילה היא בחינת עשירות, בחינת טעמה כי טוב סחרה לא יכבה בלילה נרה. כי עשירות בא משם, כדמשמע בכמה מקומות בדברי רבנו למעין שם. ועל כן תפלת ערבית רשות כנזכר לעיל. אבל האדנא קבעוה עלייהו חובה. כי עכשו אין זוכין לבחינת השגה זו אפלו בלילה, ועל כן חובה להתפלל כנזכר לעיל:
segments.en:
§ 45 — The Goblet in Binyamin's Sack: Hidden Mercy in Bitter Sorrow

This is the great bitterness when the goblet was found in Binyamin's sack — yet through this specifically, Yosef revealed himself and they were gathered together: "Yosef could not restrain himself" — and joy increased, as above. This is a hint: when a person is in great, bitter distress that twists his heart — let him know and believe that this too is for good. Certainly wondrous mercy is hidden within the bitterness. He must only cry out and pray to Hashem and wait for His mercy. Gavi'a [goblet] in gematria equals yud-gimmel ayin-bais [13 × 72] — the thirteen Mechilin d'Rachamay, the totality of all mercy and great kindness. Specifically through the goblet in Binyamin's sack (which caused such bitter distress), they were gathered together and it was revealed that the goblet is wondrous mercy — thirteen times seventy-two: the thirteen Mechilin d'Rachamay, the totality of all mercy, as above.

§ 46 — "I Rejoiced When They Said: Let Us Go to the House of Hashem"

"I rejoiced when they said to me: let us go to the house of Hashem." The essential joy is in the house of Hashem — the Bais HaMikdash, deriving from "the Place of the world": "blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place," as above. "Our feet were standing in your gates, Yerushalayim" — there is the essential standing and sustenance of the feet. The essential thing is to sort the feet, as above — but their complete sorting is when one comes on foot to the Bais HaMikdash (and likewise to the true tzadikim, who are in the aspect of the Bais HaMikdash), where the essential completeness of joy resides.

"Yerushalayim, built as a city joined together; there the tribes ascended, the tribes of G-d, a testimony to Israel, to thank the Name of Hashem." Yerushalayim below corresponds to Yerushalayim above — the above supernal Place ("he encountered the place"). There the tribes ascended — to thank [l'hodos]: all the ascents through the above tikunim are to ascend to the supernal Place, where the essential todah and thanksgiving in joy resides — "to thank the Name of Hashem."

"Pray for the peace of Yerushalayim... peace within your walls... for the sake of my brothers and friends, I shall speak of peace within you." The essential thing depends on peace, as above. Dispute is hatred and anger — sadness from the Chambers of Exchange, which exchange and reverse everything, implanting false reasoning in the heart to hate one's fellow for nothing — even among tzadikim and the upright, multiplying dispute through their reversed reasoning. This is the dispute of the tribes against Yosef the tzadik, selling him as a slave. But in the end, everything is transformed for good through the great tzadikim who know how to draw joy even in the bitterness of exile, extracting from the exile and the Chambers of Exchange, as above.

§ 47 — Yehudah and Yosef: Mashiach ben David and Mashiach ben Yosef

This is: "Yehudah approached him" — the essential tikun through Yehudah and Yosef uniting — the essence of Mashiach ben David (from Yehudah) and Mashiach ben Yosef. David is the aspect of Tehillim, composed with the ten types of melody (= joy) — the sweet singer of Israel. The inflaming of joy in the heart (= Yosef, "the house of Yosef a flame") — its essential revelation is through words of thanksgiving and praise (= David, who satiated the Holy One with songs and praises). Speech has great power — through it the essential revelation of joy: "a man has joy in the answer of his mouth"; "worry in a man's heart — let him quash it; a good word gladdens it." This is: "lips of song shall my mouth praise" specifically — the aspect of David from Yehudah, named for thanksgiving: "this time I shall thank Hashem."

Yehudah said to Yosef: "let your servant speak a word in the ears of my lord." Ears are the instrument of hearing; "hearing depends on the heart" — where the root of joy resides: "You placed joy in my heart." This joy is aroused by Yosef, who inflames the heart by blowing away the dust. But the essential revelation and sustaining of joy is through speech (= David from Yehudah). Therefore Yehudah said to Yosef: "let your servant speak a word" — specifically a word: holy words of the joy of holy emunah, as we proclaim daily: "fortunate are we — how good is our portion!" etc. "In the ears of my lord" — "hearing depends on the heart." Rashi: "let my words enter your ears." Through the speech, the words enter his ears and heart until joy shines in completeness and sadness (= anger and judgment) is nullified. "Let not your anger burn against your servant" — anger nullified through the intensity of joy shining through speech, as above.

§ 48 — Yaakov's Care That Binyamin Be Born in Eretz Yisrael

Therefore Yaakov was extremely careful that the holy bed not be completed outside Eretz Yisrael, as stated in the holy Zohar — when Yosef was born he said: "send me away." Had Binyamin been born outside Eretz Yisrael, Yaakov could not have left, as the Zohar states. Binyamin — the completion of the holy bed, the ultimate completeness of joy — through him joy is drawn from "the Place of the world" to the place of this world. The essential holy Place is the awesome place of the Bais HaMikdash. Had he been born, chas v'shalom, in the impure place of Lavan's house outside Eretz Yisrael, joy would have been drawn to the Sitra Achra, chas v'shalom — whose entire overpowering is through drawing joy to themselves: all the joys of worldly vanities (= the laughter of the fool): "of joy — what does it accomplish?" We plead: "let not my enemies rejoice over me."
segments.he_nikud: וְעַל-כֵּן יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית דַּיְקָא. כִּי אָז בַּלַּיְלָה הַזְּמַן מְסֻגָּל יוֹתֵר לְהַשָּגוֹת וְהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בש"ט שֶׁרֹב חִדּוּשֵׁי תּוֹרָה זוֹכִין בַּלַּיְלָה. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּנוּ (בְּסִימָן נב) שֶׁבַּלַּיְלָה מְסֻגָּל יוֹתֵר לְבִטּוּל עַיֵּן שָׁם. גַּם הַלַּיְלָה הִיא בְּחִינַת עֲשִׁירוּת, בְּחִינַת טָעֲמָה כִּי טוֹב סַחְרָהּ לֹא יִכְבֶּה בַלַּיְלָה נֵרָהּ. כִּי עֲשִׁירוּת בָּא מִשָּׁם, כִּדְמַשְׁמַע בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת בְּדִבְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ לַמְעַיֵּן שָׁם. וְעַל-כֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. אֲבָל הָאִדָּנָָא קְבָעוּהָ עָלַייהוּ חוֹבָה. כִּי עַכְשָׁו אֵין זוֹכִין לִבְחִינַת הַשָּגָה זוֹ אֲפִלּוּ בַּלַּיְלָה, וְעַל-כֵּן חוֹבָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:

segments.he: ועל-כן בערב מברך שתים לפני קריאת שמע ושתים לאחריה . אבל בשחר אין מברכין כי אם שלש ברכות שתים לפניה ואחת לאחריה. כי ערבית שהוא כנגד יעקב שזכה לנחלה בלי מצרים בחינת ופרצת ימה וקדמה צפנה ונגבה . וכנגד זה מברכין ארבע ברכות לפני קריאת שמע ולאחריה כנגד ד' רוחות העולם. כי זוכין אז לנחלת יעקב נחלה בלי מצרים. אבל בשחרית אין מברכין כי אם שלש ברכות כנגד שלש רוחות של בנין העולם, כי צפון חסר . ושם התגברות הסטרא אחרא בחינת מצפון תפתח וכו' . כי שחרית הוא כנגד אברהם, שהוא בימיו עדין לא הכניע לגמרי הסטרא אחרא ולא זכה עדין לנחלה בלי מצרים. אבל יעקב זכה להכניעה לגמרי וזכה לכבש כל ארבע רוחות העולם אפלו רוח צפון. ומאחר שהכניע את רוח צפון על כן זכה לעשירות גדול שעקרו בא משם, בחינת מצפון זהב יאתה, ועל כן הוסיפו ברכה רביעית בערבית שהיא נתקנה כנגד בחינת יעקב כנזכר לעיל, והוא ברכת השכיבנו. ועל כן מבקשין אז ופרוס עלינו סכת שלומך, שהוא בחינת יעקב, בחינת ויעקב נסע סכתה . וזהו שמבקשין אז על התעוררות השנה כמו שאומרים והעמידנו מלכנו וכו'. כי על ידי זה זוכין לבחינת יראה כמו שמבאר שם בדברי רבנו עין שם היטב. וזהו ותקננו בעצה טובה מלפניך. כי על ידי התעוררות השנה בא כח הדבור לכלי ההולדה שהם כליות יועצות. עין שם היטב:
segments.en:
Therefore he ensured the holy bed was completed through Binyamin's birth — so joy would be drawn to its proper place, Eretz Yisrael and the Bais HaMikdash, where holy joy in Him resides. From there we can draw holy joy even now in exile, outside Eretz Yisrael. Wherever Israel is exiled, they draw the holiness of Eretz Yisrael through shuls and batay midrash (= a miniature Mikdash), and essentially through the power of the true tzadikim, as above.

§ 49 — David Found the Place: The Ge'ulah Through Mashiach ben David

Therefore the essential finding of that awesome Place was through David specifically, who labored and toiled exceedingly to find it: "remember, Hashem, for David all his affliction... if I enter my tent... if I give sleep to my eyes... until I find a place for Hashem." He was the sweet singer of Israel, engaged in words of songs and praises always — through which the awesome Place is essentially revealed, where His G-dliness is revealed, which is all our joy. Therefore the essential ge'ulah will be through Mashiach ben David, encompassing both David and Yosef, as is known. Every Jew must draw upon himself at all times the holiness of joy in Him through holy words, as above.

§ 50 — Birchas HaNisim: The Blessing over Miracles "In This Place"

This is the aspect of Birchas HaNisim — the blessing recited when arriving at a place where a miracle was performed for oneself or for our forefathers, as stated in the Shulchan Aruch (siman 218): one who sees a place where miracles were performed for our forefathers blesses: "blessed is He who performed miracles for our forefathers in this place." When arriving at a place where a miracle was performed for oneself: "blessed is He who performed a miracle for me in this place." Our Sages specified that the place be mentioned in the blessing — "in this place" specifically.

All miracles derive from that Place — the place of the Bais HaMikdash, whose awesome holiness derives from the above supernal Place (= Keser): "blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place." From the obstructer (called Place) many tzimtzumim descended until this physical place came into being — the dust of the earth upon which we stand in this World of Action. Here resides all our free will — for which everything was created. For the sake of free will, the Sitra Achra (= the Chambers of Exchange) clings to this physical place — wanting to exchange and reverse everything from good to evil, from truth to falsehood, etc. Man's essential service: to stand the test, not follow the counsel of the wicked who reverse everything through their reasoning, but cling to the true tzadikim and follow their counsel, until he merits his eternal purpose.

The essential power of the Chambers of Exchange to mislead is according to the flaw in the Arranger and Settler of the mind (= the obstructer, the aspect of Place) — due to which one lacks the yishuv hada'as to overpower properly, to look at the truth and walk the true path. This derives from not yet meriting the tikun of the supernal Arranger and Settler. In the matter of the pursuit and obstructer — from which one perceives what one perceives — everything depends. Even awesome, great tzadikim flawed in this by not properly rectifying the Arranger and Settler — pursuing excessively and breaking through to ascend to Hashem: the flaw of Nadav and Avihu, "when they drew near before Hashem and died," as above. The aspect of: "he peeked and was stricken; he peeked and died." This was the essential sin of Adam HaRishon, as the holy Zohar states: he gazed at what he had no permission to gaze at. He flawed greatly — following the serpent's counsel, drawn after the desire of eating from the Tree of Knowledge (where the Chambers of Exchange essentially cling: "the flaming, revolving sword"). Not only that, they gazed above at what they had no permission: "the tree was good for eating, desirable to the eyes, and coveted to make wise" — the serpent enticed them to pursue their desires and gaze at lofty wisdoms and perceptions they had no permission to gaze at, especially after such flaws. This is the flaw of all the philosophers and false-wisdoms of today — pursuing all desires (eating, drinking, immorality, money, honor, anger, contentiousness, etc.) yet wanting to understand, intellectualize, and gaze at His G-dliness and His ways of governance — until they went astray as they went astray. All this is the flaw of the Arranger and Settler of the mind. From this come all troubles and sufferings, chas v'shalom — the Chambers of Exchange overpowering, from which all dangers and troubles, chas v'shalom.

When Hashem has mercy and performs a miracle, the essential miracle derives — through the power of the great tzadikim — from that Place where the above nine chambers are perceived (not clinging, not known, etc.) — above the intellect. From there come all miracles — which are above the intellect. Intellect dictates that things should follow nature (the sea remains sea, dry land remains dry land), but when Hashem performs a miracle — splitting the sea into dry land — this is above the intellect. Therefore the philosophers, who do not nullify their minds, do not believe in miracles, laboring to deny them, chas v'shalom — despite our having seen countless miracles and wonders with our own eyes.

Therefore all miracles derive from the above nine chambers (from Keser, the tikun of the Arranger, etc. = the aspect of Place). These nine chambers are above the intellect — not clinging, not known. In truth, all miracles derive from the Bais HaMikdash, where ten miracles occurred. The essential holiness of the Bais HaMikdash is the tenth holiness — Keser, the aspect of Place — from which all miracles in the world derive. Therefore when Israel left Egypt with wondrous miracles and the sea was split, they sang: "You shall bring them and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance" — the Bais HaMikdash, from which the essential miracles of the Exodus and the splitting of the sea derive. The essential purpose was to come there: "He brought us out from there to bring us to..." etc., as explained elsewhere.

Therefore when a miracle is performed, one must bless: "who performed a miracle for me in this place" — mentioning the place specifically. The essential miracle in this place derives from the awesome holiness of the root of the Place — the above Arranger, from which the nine chambers (not clinging, etc.) derive — from which all miracles come, as above.

segments.he_nikud: וְעַל-כֵּן בָּעֶרֶב מְבָרֵךְ שְׁתַּיִם לִפְנֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּשְׁתַּיִם לְאַחֲרֶיהָ. אֲבָל בַּשַּׁחַר אֵין מְבָרְכִין כִּי אִם שָׁלֹשׁ בְּרָכוֹת שְׁתַּיִם לְפָנֶיהָ וְאַחַת לְאַחֲרֶיהָ. כִּי עַרְבִית שֶׁהִוא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב שֶׁזָּכָה לְנַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים בְּחִינַת וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה צָפֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה. וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה מְבָרְכִין אַרְבַּע בְּרָכוֹת לִפְנֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ כְּנֶגֶד ד' רוּחוֹת הָעוֹלָם. כִּי זוֹכִין אָז לְנַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים. אֲבָל בְּשַׁחֲרִית אֵין מְבָרְכִין כִּי אִם שָׁלֹשׁ בְּרָכוֹת כְּנֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹת שֶׁל בִּנְיַן הָעוֹלָם, כִּי צָפוֹן חָסֵר. וְשָׁם הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא בְּחִינַת מִצָּפוֹן תִּפָּתַח וְכוּ'. כִּי שַׁחֲרִית הוּא כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם, שֶׁהוּא בְּיָמָיו עֲדַיִן לֹא הִכְנִיעַ לְגַמְרֵי הַסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא וְלֹא זָכָה עֲדַיִן לְנַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים. אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב זָכָה לְהַכְנִיעָהּ לְגַמְרֵי וְזָכָה לִכְבֹּשׁ כָּל אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֲפִלּוּ רוּחַ צָפוֹן. וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהִכְנִיעַ אֶת רוּחַ צָפוֹן עַל-כֵּן זָכָה לַעֲשִׁירוּת גָּדוֹל שֶׁעִקָּרוֹ בָּא מִשָּׁם, בְּחִינַת מִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶאֱתֶה, וְעַל-כֵּן הוֹסִיפוּ בְּרָכָה רְבִיעִית בְּעַרְבִית שֶׁהִיא נִתְקְנָה כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וְהִוא בִּרְכַּת הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ. וְעַל-כֵּן מְבַקְּשִׁין אָז וּפְְרוֹס עָלֵינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶךָ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב, בְּחִינַת וְיַעֲקֹב נָסַע סֻכֹּתָה. וְזֶהוּ שֶׁמְּבַקְּשִׁין אָז עַל הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשֵּׁנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים וְהַעֲמִידֵנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ וְכוּ'. כִּי עַל-יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לִבְחִינַת יִרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר שָׁם בְּדִבְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ עַיֵּן שָׁם הֵיטֵב. וְזֶהוּ וְתַקְּנֵנוּ בְּעֵצָה טוֹבָה מִלְּפָנֶיךָ. כִּי עַל-יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשֵּׁנָה בָּא כֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר לִכְלֵי הַהוֹלָדָה שֶׁהֵם כְּלָיוֹת יוֹעֲצוֹת. עַיֵּן שָׁם הֵיטֵב:
